alignments.note: out realizes the ἐξ- prefix; discontinuous under rule 15.
Rule 40: a subordinating element takes whatever word introduces its English clause, and nothing more. The supplied subject and copula belong to the predicate, not to the clause-introducer.

Rules 62 and 68: the clause expresses no subject, and where the ASV supplies both a subject pronoun and a copula the prepositional predicate carries them. Rule 62 heads such a unit on the word realizing the preposition, so the head is over rather than the supplied were. Reading until they were as one unit on ἕως is the competing analysis, but rule 53 refuses to read a supplied copula off English word order, and πρὸς Βηθανίαν is the predicate left in the clause to carry it.
up is the verb's own particle.
Rule 20: displaced by his, which belongs to αὐτοῦ.
Rule 88: the juncture and belongs to the finite verb it introduces.

review_notes: Corrected s004/s005: the accepted alignment gave until they were to ἕως and only over against to πρός. Rules 53, 62 and 68 decide a supplied verb by what is left in the clause to carry it, and what is left here is the expressed prepositional predicate πρὸς Βηθανίαν, not the subordinator; rule 53 names giving such a copula to the word the ASV writes it next to as the recurring failure.
The head stays on over rather than on the supplied were, as rule 62 requires for a preposition carrier.
